# Data profile

*Generated by `pipeline/profile_data.py` on 2026-10-15. Do not edit by hand; rerun the script.*

This report describes the raw data **before any cleaning**. It answers: what is in each file, how the files overlap, and what looks odd. Rule IDs (C6, T0, V1, ...) refer to `docs/methodology.md`.

> FairAssess NJ is an independent student research project that uses public data. It is not legal, tax, or appraisal advice. Homeowners file and present their own appeals. Confirm deadlines, fees, and forms with the Bergen County Board of Taxation.


## 1. The SR1A files

SR1A is the state's sales file. Every deed recorded in New Jersey gets one line of 663 characters.

| File | File date | Rows (all NJ) | Rows (Bergen) | First recorded | Last recorded | Earliest deed | Latest deed | Layout matches PDF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales2024 | 2024-09-24 | 167,598 | 13,580 | 2023-07-03 | 2024-06-28 | 2007-11-26 | 2024-06-27 | **no** |
| Sales2025 | 2025-09-22 | 171,949 | 14,003 | 2024-07-01 | 2025-06-30 | 2015-10-01 | 2025-06-27 | yes |
| YTDSR1A2026 | 2026-08-12 | 169,935 | 13,536 | 2025-07-01 | 2026-06-30 | 2023-02-07 | 2026-06-26 | yes |
| Sales2026 | 2026-09-24 | 170,664 | 14,012 | 2025-07-01 | 2026-06-30 | 2023-02-07 | 2026-06-26 | yes |

- Every line in every file is exactly 663 characters long. No file has two exactly identical lines.
- "Recorded" is the date the deed was filed with the county. Each file covers **July 1 to June 30** of recording dates. That is the state's own sampling year (methodology Section 3.2).
- "Deed" is the date the deed was signed. A few deeds are years old when they are finally recorded (the earliest in Sales2026 was signed 2023-02-07), so deed dates spread wider than recording dates.

**Sales2024 does not match the layout PDF.** Its value fields are shifted: in most Bergen rows, positions 65-73 hold land + building (the total), not the building value, and its SALES-RATIO only matches our math on a minority of rows. Its property class sits one place to the right, and its ETC flag is "X" on every Bergen row. Dates (positions 339-350) and the county/town codes still line up, so the table above is right, but the parser does **not** decode Sales2024 into the parquet file. Sales2024 is not used in v1 (methodology Section 3.1).

### Duplicates across files

Each SR1A line has a SERIAL-NUMBER, which the state calls a "unique auto generated number issued to each SR1A." We use **record_id = county code + district code + serial number** (for example `0201-7354015`). No record_id repeats inside any file.

| Pair of files | Shared sales | Only in first | Only in second |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales2026 and YTDSR1A2026 | 13,536 | 476 | 0 |
| Sales2025 and Sales2026 | 0 | 14,003 | 14,012 |

What this shows:
- **YTDSR1A2026 is an older copy of Sales2026.** Every one of its 13,536 Bergen sales is also in Sales2026. Its file date is August 12, 2026; Sales2026's is September 24, 2026. Sales2026 has 476 more sales, 241 of them recorded in June 2026 (late arrivals).
- Of the 13,536 shared sales, 12,740 lines are identical. The rest were updated by the state between the two copies. 555 sales changed from usable to non-usable, and 7 changed the other way.
- **Rule for removing duplicates:** when the same record_id is in two files, keep the row from the newer file (Sales2026). The parquet file keeps every row and marks the older copy with `superseded_by_newer_file = True`, so nothing is thrown away before the cleaning step.
- Sales2025 and Sales2026 share no sales. Their recording dates do not overlap.

**For the rest of this report** we use the 28,015 Bergen rows that are not superseded: Sales2025 (14,003) plus Sales2026 (14,012). Recording dates run July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2026, which is exactly 24 months.

### Towns assessed far below market value

A ratio far below 1.0 does **not** by itself mean a town is unfair. New Jersey towns do not all assess at 100% of market value. Between revaluations, home prices rise but assessments stay the same, so the ratio drifts down over time. What matters for fairness is whether homes *within* a town have similar ratios (COD) and whether cheap and expensive homes are treated alike (PRD, PRB). That is why every comparison on the site is made against each town's own level.

- 31 towns have a median raw ratio under 0.70: Garfield (0.44), Lodi (0.46), Fair Lawn (0.47), Bergenfield (0.49), Ridgewood (0.52), Upper Saddle River (0.53), Midland Park (0.53), Glen Rock (0.55), Haworth (0.55), Park Ridge (0.57), Leonia (0.57), Englewood (0.57), Montvale (0.57), Emerson (0.57), Hillsdale (0.58), Tenafly (0.58), Northvale (0.58), Rutherford (0.60), Mahwah (0.60), Harrington Park (0.60), Cliffside Park (0.60), Elmwood Park (0.61), Wood-Ridge (0.62), Rochelle Park (0.62), Fort Lee (0.62), Washington Township (0.63), River Vale (0.64), Ho-Ho-Kus (0.64), Franklin Lakes (0.64), Hackensack (0.68), Wyckoff (0.68).
- The lowest is Garfield at 0.44: a typical home there is assessed at about 44% of its sale price. The state's 2027 average ratio for Garfield (47.06%) tells the same story.
- No town has a median raw ratio above 1.0.
- Using Sales2026 only (the state's sampling year), our raw median is below the state's 2027 average ratio in 68 of 69 towns with sales. The average gap is -6.7 points and the biggest is -30.2 points. Methodology rule V3 expects our median to sit below the state's number. (These raw medians still include condos and multi-lot sales.)
- The 5 biggest gaps (Sales2026 only): Rockleigh (-30.2), Carlstadt (-22.8), Elmwood Park (-15.6), South Hackensack (-14.1), Rochelle Park (-13.5). 5 of these 5 towns are on the county's 2026 revaluation/reassessment list. In 2026-list towns, 0 usable class-2 Sales2026 sales carry the old (ASSESS-YEAR 25) assessment, so the gap is **not** caused by mixing old and new assessments. Several of these towns have very few sales (Rockleigh 2, Carlstadt 10, Elmwood Park 38, South Hackensack 2, Rochelle Park 16). We do not yet know why the gap is so large; rule V3 flags these towns for review once cleaning is done. **Decided (methodology 1.1, rule C6):** a sale is multi-lot when TOTAL ASSESSMENT is greater than the main-lot total.
- The 24-month medians (table above) mix two assessment bases in the 36 towns on the 2026 list: 1,363 of their 1,363 usable class-2 Sales2025 sales carry a pre-revaluation assessment (ASSESS-YEAR before 26). This helps explain why, for example, Leonia's 24-month median is far below its 2027 state ratio. Rule C9 handles this; town statistics use Sales2026 only (rule T0).
- 4 towns have fewer than 20 sales even over 24 months: Moonachie, Rockleigh, South Hackensack, Teterboro.

## 6. Surprises and questions for the methodology

### 6.1 "00000" placeholders in ADDL-BLOCK (affects rule C6)

Rule C6 says a sale is multi-lot if "any ADDL-BLOCK(1) to ADDL-BLOCK(5) is not blank." In **Sales2025**, 881 usable class-2 sales have ADDL-BLOCK(1) = "00000" with no extra lot and $0 extra value. It is a placeholder, not a real lot. Read literally, C6 would wrongly drop them. Sales2026 has no such placeholders.

| File | ADDL-BLOCK not blank | ADDL-BLOCK not blank and not 00000 | ADDL-VALUE-TOTAL > 0 | TOTAL ASSESSMENT > main lot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales2025 | 918 | 37 | 37 | 37 |
| Sales2026 | 21 | 21 | 21 | 21 |

Three tests agree on every one of the 10,212 usable class-2 sales (10,212 of 10,212) once "00000" is treated as blank. TOTAL ASSESSMENT (positions 5-16) always equals the main lot plus the extra lots (28,015 of 28,015 rows). **Decided (methodology 1.1, rule C6):** multi-lot sales are still dropped, not kept with TOTAL ASSESSMENT.

### 6.2 TOTAL ASSESSMENT covers every lot in the sale

Positions 5-16 hold TOTAL ASSESSMENT (the 2011 description PDF has BATCH-NUMBER and DLN there instead). For one-lot sales it equals the main-lot assessment. For multi-lot sales it adds the extra lots. The state's own SALES-RATIO uses this total for multi-lot sales (174 of 176 multi-lot sales priced $1,000 or more; 2 use the main lot only). This means multi-lot sales could be **kept** (using TOTAL ASSESSMENT) instead of dropped. Logged in `docs/validation.md` to investigate in the validation step.

### 6.3 YTDSR1A2026 is an older copy of Sales2026

It is a subset taken six weeks earlier. Later state reviews turned some usable sales into non-usable ones. This supports methodology Section 3.1: use Sales2026, not YTDSR1A2026.

### 6.4 Date formats are mixed

DEED-DATE, DATE-RECORDED, and AGING-DATE read as YYMMDD. LAST-UPDATE-DATE reads as **MMDDYY** (values like 122925 cannot be YYMMDD). The description PDF says the opposite for both. The parser handles each field by its real format and has tests for both.

### 6.5 Assessment year paired with each sale (usable class 2)

| Recorded | ASSESS-YEAR 24 | ASSESS-YEAR 25 | ASSESS-YEAR 26 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 Jul-Dec | 2,202 | 0 | 0 |
| 2025 Jan-Jun | 571 | 2,522 | 0 |
| 2025 Jul-Dec | 0 | 2,323 | 0 |
| 2026 Jan-Jun | 0 | 262 | 2,332 |

Sales recorded July to December carry the current year's assessment; most sales recorded January to June carry the new year's assessment, but some carry the prior year. This matches methodology rule C5 (we keep the state's pairing).

### 6.6 Other notes

- **Condos:** 1,075 of the 4,917 usable class-2 sales in Sales2026 are condo units (QUALIFICATION-CODE starts with "C"). Rule C10 removes them.
- **REALTY-TRANSFER-FEE** is stored two different ways (whole dollars in Sales2025; with a written decimal point and one extra character in Sales2026). We do not use it, so the parser does not keep it.
- **2026AvgResStat.pdf** has an "Avg Tax Bill" column, but it is **empty for all 70 Bergen towns**. The table keeps the column (blank). The checker's savings estimate uses GTRhistory.xlsx instead (rule K12).
- **Tax rates:** GTRhistory.xlsx runs 1997 to **2025**. There is no 2026 rate, and no separate 2026 Bergen tax rate file in `data/raw/state/`. Rule K12 already uses 2025.
- **State coefficient table:** CoefficientDeviations.pdf has 2023-2026 for all 70 towns; 5 town-years are marked amended (*).
